title: Adding Lucene-style ?q= query string search for alerts made the Postgres backend build WHERE clauses by str.format()-ing user search terms into SQL.

findings.explanation: User‑controlled field names (e.g. self.tokens.field[0] or self.tokens.fieldname) are interpolated directly into the generated SQL string without allow‑listing or quoting, while only the values are parameterised. If an attacker can influence the field name via the query syntax, they could inject arbitrary SQL identifiers or clauses.

evidence.content:
elif self.tokens.attr:
    tokens_attr = self.tokens.attr.replace('_', 'attributes')
    p_key = _next_param(params)
    params[p_key] = self.tokens.fieldname
    p_val = _next_param(params)
    params[p_val] = f'%{self.tokens.singleterm}%'
    return f'"{tokens_attr}"::jsonb ->>%({p_key})s ILIKE %({p_val})s'
else:
    p = _next_param(params)
    params[p] = f'%{self.tokens.singleterm}%'
    return f'"{self.tokens.field[0]}" ILIKE %({p})s'

findings.suggested_fix: Validate and whitelist allowed field names before interpolating them into the SQL string, or use identifier‑parameterisation mechanisms (e.g., psycopg2.sql.Identifier) to safely quote field names.

findings.explanation: The changes only affect query parsing and parameter handling; no new endpoint, resource lookup, or permission check is introduced or modified.
